# ClodHub

> ClodHub is a catalogue of reviewed components and recipes that AI agents assemble into apps with aepm. A component is a reviewed part of an application; a recipe lists the components an application needs, the questions that choose between them and how they connect. Developers sign in with GitHub and publish from their own repositories; anyone reads the catalogue without a key.

- [API reference for agents](https://clodhub.com/agents.md): every endpoint, publishing with `Authorization: Bearer ch_...`.
- [Repository contract](https://clodhub.com/contract.md): what a recipe or component repository implements, and the catalogue publish API.
- [Package foundations](https://clodhub.com/docs/package-foundations.md): the licence, source, compatibility and file facts every package declares.
- [Building on GitHub with no machine of your own](https://clodhub.com/cloud-assembly.md): aepm in GitHub Actions from a committed `answers.json` (workflow https://clodhub.com/aepm-assemble.yml), then the recipe's check, release and update workflows, and the secrets they need.
- [Free services for small organisations' apps](https://clodhub.com/free-tiers.md): video, realtime, databases, AI and more on free plans, with agent setup steps.
- Review policy: https://clodhub.com/policy/levelnpolicy.json holds Level N's release and guardian keys for aepm's owner policy.
- What a download is: a component package is the source code itself (one `.tar` archive: the implementation per device or server, its contract, tests and a manifest listing every file), not a link to code. A recipe package is `recipe.json` (questions, slots, settings) plus the recipe's own application code, artwork and text; the components that fill its slots are separate downloads. Archives are release files on the publisher's public GitHub repository; ClodHub keeps a pointer and the sha256 digest, never the code. aepm checks the digest and runs none of the package's code when installing.
- Recipes: https://clodhub.com/recipes (plain text: /recipes.txt, JSON: /api/recipes). Search and filter: `/api/recipes?q=&category=&platform=&quality=&certified=&channel=&secure=&sort=` (cursor pages of 30). A recipe's build steps, questions (with `askWhen` and the settings each answer sets), slots (each with `includedWhen`), jobs and components: `/recipes/<name>.txt`; its description, slot classes, suitability, guardians, connections, tested answers and package foundations: `/recipes/<name>/details.txt`. Build from one with aepm (https://github.com/clodhub/aepm): `aepm fetch <recipe>@<version> --with-dependencies`, `aepm questions`, `aepm design`, `aepm doctor`, `aepm resolve`, `aepm install`, `aepm verify --trusted`; the steps are on each recipe's .txt page and in /agents.md; no single command runs them all. Its bundle link is `/api/recipes/<name>/<version>/bundle`.
- Components: https://clodhub.com/components (plain text: /components.txt, JSON: /api/components). Filter by `class=`, `provides=`, `requires=`, `category=`, `platform=`, `quality=`, `certified=`, `channel=`, `secure=true`, `deprecated=exclude|include|only`; search with `q=`; sort by `downloads`, `trending`, `updated`, `name` or `relevance`. Classes: https://clodhub.com/classes (each with its implementations side by side); category tree: /categories.txt. Known vulnerabilities per version: `/api/components/<name>/<version>/vulnerabilities`. A component's class, interfaces, platforms, toolchains, settings and the recipe slot that names it: `/components/<name>.txt`; its upstream sources, exact dependencies and file lists: `/components/<name>/details.txt`.
- Slots: `class` is exactly `{name,version,digest}`, resolved from independent inline declarations in the recipe package's `classes`. Each descriptor owns interfaces, platform modules, settings and shared behaviour suites with file/digest inventories. A candidate lists the exact reference in `implements`, carries the same descriptor, satisfies ports/settings/modules and has compatible platforms, runtimes, frameworks, dependency pins and styles. `aepm alternatives <recipe>@<version> <slot> --store store` lists fitting implementations; `aepm design ... --substitute <slot>=<name>@<version>` selects one.
- Publication requires `foundations:{licence,platforms,classes,implements,upstream,compatibility,maintenance,files,artefacts}` from the validated canonical package manifest. Wrapper and upstream licences remain distinct; upstream delivery states bundled source or an exact build-time dependency with its npm, Gradle or Swift lock. Public facts are publisher-declared (`foundationEvidence` is `publisher-declared`); a version gives a `foundations` summary with counts, and `/api/{recipes,components}/<name>/<version>/details` the full lists. The Worker checks descriptor hashes and declared structure; aepm checks archive bytes, selected answers and signed review evidence. Field mapping: /contract.md, Package foundations.
- Deprecated and orphaned entries: every recipe and component response, page and `.txt` carries a `deprecations` array (and a `DEPRECATION WARNING:` line in text) for the entry and the components it uses. A recipe's full tree: `/api/recipes/<name>/<version>/deprecations`. Search for replacements or similar recipes, or decide never to update. An orphaned entry's publisher deleted their account; its bundle link says `bundle-unavailable` unless the release is public.
- Sitemap: https://clodhub.com/sitemap.xml
- Developer page: https://clodhub.com/dev (sign in with GitHub; API keys and the GitHub token).
- Delivering a finished application to people's devices is a separate service: https://ourapps.app/llms.txt.
- Source: https://github.com/clodhub/clodhub
